probes.text: Rickard et al. (2001) developed a fluorescent quantitative multiplex PCR dosage assay for EYA1 exons 7, 9, and 13. probes.text: Ohno et al. (2002) identified an asn88-to-lys (N88K) mutation in TPR3 of the RAPSN gene in all 4 of their patients with CMS and endplate AChR deficiency. checks.explanation: The patient carries N88K and 553ins5. Compound heterozygosity is implied by the recessive inheritance but not stated outright, and the abstract does not describe 553ins5 as a 5-bp insertion beyond its name.

probes.text: Xiang et al. (1999) studied a French family with autosomal dominant myopathy whose clinical and muscle biopsy findings were similar to those of the Swedish families mapped to 2q24-q31. The 2q24-q31 region was completely excluded in this family. A genome-wide scan with polymorphic microsatellite markers gave a maximum 2-point lod score of 2.11, the highest possible in this family, for markers in a 4-cM region between D2S1272 and D2S1260. The authors suggested that the gene for the French form probably lies on chromosome 2q21.

probes.text: Muller et al. (2014) sequenced UNC13D, STX11, and STXBP2 in 3 patients with FHL4 from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families. The parents were heterozygous and had no history of inflammatory disease. Syntaxin-11 expression was greatly reduced in cells from 1 patient. In transfected cells, the L58P mutant failed to bind Munc18-2 (see PATHOGENESIS).
